text:
maria: Heads up — we've got ~18 pods Pending in us-west-2-gpu and the cluster-autoscaler didn't spin up any new nodes.
kevin: Same. Events show `0/18 nodes are available: 18 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` even though there are spare CPUs on existing nodes.
arjun: Can you paste `kubectl describe pod <one-pending-pod>`? I want to see requests/limits and nodeSelector.
maria: pasted below:
```
Containers:
  model-server:
    Requests:
      cpu: 2000m
      memory: 8Gi
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    Limits:
      cpu: 4000m
      memory: 12Gi
Node-Selectors: accelerator: nvidia-t4
Tolerations: <none>
```
kevin: Ah — nodeSelector `accelerator: nvidia-t4` is the culprit. We recently renamed the label to `gpu-type: t4` during the nodepool rollout. CA won't consider nodes that don't match.
lisa: Also noticed the GPU device-plugin on the new nodes reports allocatable GPUs=0 for a short window after driver pod startup. If a pending pod is evaluated during that window CA decides there's no capacity.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: driver-daemonset v1.12 rolled to us-west-2-gpu at 12:02 UTC
arjun: Two things to do now: 1) remove the outdated nodeSelector from the failing job templates (or add fallback label), 2) bump the autoscaler's `scaleUpDelay` to 30s? or set `--node-group-auto-discovery` to include the new label mapping so CA can propose new nodes. Also we should set `check-additional-pods` to true so CA re-evaluates after driver readiness.
maria: Quick mitigation applied: removed nodeSelector from the failing jobs and added `gpu-type: t4` label to a staging node. Pending count dropped to 4, CA started a scale-up for the dedicated-gpu-pool.
kevin: For long term: we should avoid hard nodeSelectors for accelerator type. Use nodeAffinity with preferredDuringScheduling or support label aliases in our deployment tooling. Also consider switching to MIG slices (T4/MIG) or enabling fractional GPU sharing for smaller workloads to reduce fragmentation.
lisa: Cost note — autoscaling into on-demand p4 instances will spike monthly spend. Let's enable spot pools as burst capacity for non-critical training and use Dedicated for latency-sensitive inference.
arjun: Filed infra ticket INF-4123 to: 1) reconcile node labels across regions, 2) adjust CA flags (`--scan-interval=10s`, `--balance-similar-node-groups=true`, `--check-additional-pods=true`), 3) add a small integration test that deploys a GPU pod after driver DS rolling updates. Assigning to SRE squad.
maria: Thanks. I'll watch the queue and follow up if more pods pop back to Pending.
kevin: 👍 keep an eye on binpacking — we still have some nodes with 1 GPU free but unusable because pods request 2 GPUs. Let's add a recommendation in runbooks to prefer 1-GPU containers or use a scheduler extender for better binpacking.
lisa: adding cost/ops checklist to the ticket now.
